title: Book Two · Chapter 12: The Basket Goes Home
story:
On Friday, six children sit beside Miss Wu's desk. Ronan and Leo have their story pages. Mei and Jun share another copy. Two other children sit at the end.

Miss Wu puts her cup out of the way.

“Ronan, please begin.”

He holds the page high. He reads about the girl and her brother. The girl carries a basket to the shop. Her brother holds the door. The girl chooses flowers. At the end, the two children go home.

Ronan reaches the bottom first. He puts the page on his knees.

“Finished.”

Leo is still near the last line. Ronan tries not to look too pleased.

Miss Wu turns to the group.

“Who carries the basket home?”

“The girl,” Ronan says.

Jun looks at his page. He puts one finger on the last line.

“I think it is her brother.”

“The girl has it at the start.”

“Yes,” Mei says. “But she buys flowers.”

“She can have both.”

Mei lifts both hands like the girl in the picture. The flowers are big. The girl holds them with both arms.

“Where can she put a basket?”

Ronan looks down. He finds the first line at once. The basket is there. But Miss Wu is waiting for the end of the story.

Jun points to the last line.

Ronan reads it aloud.

“The brother carries the basket home.”

He moves his thumb away from the edge. There is the whole line. He read it a minute ago. He remembered the girl at the start. He did not check the last line for his answer.

“Oh,” he says. “They change things.”

“The girl carries the flowers,” Jun says.

“And her brother carries the basket,” Ronan adds.

Miss Wu puts two simple marks on the board. One is a basket. One is a large bunch of flowers. She draws the same pictures on two small cards.

“Show us the walk home.”

Mei takes the flower mark on a small card. Jun takes the basket card. They walk two steps together. The group can see both things clearly.

Leo asks to be the shop door.

“You need to stay here, then,” Mei says. “Doors do not walk home.”

Leo holds one arm out. Jun pushes past very carefully. The two children at the end laugh.

Miss Wu lets them finish the little scene. Then she gives the next part to another child. Ronan puts his page down and listens.

The last child reads slowly. Ronan opens his mouth. He wants to say the next word. Miss Wu lifts a finger. He closes his mouth. The child finds the word and continues.

After the group, Jun picks up the basket card. One corner is bent.

“We can keep this for the book corner,” he says.

Ronan helps flatten it under a heavy book. He holds the book at one end. Jun holds the other.

“I thought it stayed with the girl,” Ronan says.

“I did at first, too.”

“You did?”

Jun nods. “Then I saw her flowers.”

Outside, Leo waits with their ball. He holds it with both arms and looks at the school bags.

“I can carry the ball,” he says. “Who can carry me?”

“No one,” Ronan says. He takes his own bag and runs after him.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

basket＝篮子；brother＝弟弟；flowers＝花；last＝最后的。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan最初认为是谁把篮子拿回家？
2. Jun和Mei怎样帮助小组核对？

## 读句子

**Jun / points to / the last line.** Jun／指向／最后一行。
